title: Middlehelm Wetlands Ruins

camera.notes: First person. Grade at eye height walking the nave and aisle, not from an orbit camera. Waterline, joints, and vault soffits must read at 0.5–2 m. Arcade rhythm and west front read at 12–20 m.

grid.exceptionRule: Organic roots, reed, and rubble may miss the grid; their sockets and anchors snap. Structural walls, piers, floors, and vaults stay on 0.5–8 m.

units.sourceNote: Scale adapter later. Do not model a second kit in inches.

world.place: A drowned austere abbey in the Middlehelm lowlands, founded at three springs in wet forest. Pale stone on a Bernardine plan, now occupied by standing water, reed, and temperate trees.
world.whoLived: A reforming order, Cistercian in all but name. They drained the basin to keep a dry church in a wet country. Architecture as devotion: proportion, light, almost no grotesque.
world.whatHappened: The drains lost. Springs and peat reclaimed the nave. Roofs wicked out. Vaults failed as bays, some still on corbels, some lying among trees. Not a siege ruin.
world.playerPath: FPS entry at the west front or a wounded aisle, through unvaulted then vaulted bays, under the arcade, along a wet 2 m aisle, to a pooled crossing. Eye 1.7 m.
world.scaleOfSpace: Walkable nave. Standard bay 4 m, wide bay 8 m, aisle 2 m, pier 1 m, trim 0.5 m. Full 70 m church is a later layout target, not the first assembly.

artDirection.silhouette: Heavy, calm, sacred verticals. Pointed arcade at distance; round west triplet as softness. Ruin reads as missing vault plus standing arcade, with trees breaking the skyline inside the plan.
artDirection.materialStory: One stone family: pale warm limestone, wet and dry as states of the same ashlar. Timber only as shores and lost-roof ghosts. Vegetation is overlay. Metal almost absent.
artDirection.wear: Standing water ~0.35 m, stain at 1.0 m on every wall. Algae on the first courses. Vault soffits cleaner than open wall-heads. Fallen bays land as readable slabs, not noise. Hand-wear only on a surviving west-to-crossing path.
artDirection.modularityWithoutStamp: 4 m bay plus 8 m wide bay from Trois-Fontaines nave irregularity. Collapse pieces still socket. Ivy/root/reed/tree overlays. Waterline trim continuous. Plan stays orthogonal; organic sits in the plan.
artDirection.referencesHowToUse: Steal bay rhythm, arcade vs aisle, round west triplet, corbelled remaining vaults, fallen vaults as objects, trees in the nave, austere capitals, pale stone, drained-basin-returned-to-water.
artDirection.referencesHowNotToCopy: Do not photogrammetry the Marne site or kit the 18th-century abbatial gateway. Grammar, not a postcard of France.

references.name: Abbaye de Trois-Fontaines (church ruins)
references.notes: Cistercian church 1160–1190, ~70×40 m, first three bays wider, pointed arcade, pointed barrel aisles, round west triplet, rose remnant, vaults on corbels, collapsed bays among beeches. Founded 1118; monks drained the woodland.

references.name: Abbaye de Trois-Fontaines — site
references.notes: Standing ruin in park; use church ruin only. Ignore later classical gate as kit language.

references.name: 18th-century abbatial gateway (Trois-Fontaines)
references.notes: Corinthian pilasters, concave cour d'honneur. Later occupation. Not Middlehelm kit.

sockets.rule: 4 m wall/arcade mates on grid; pivot at floor, left-hand as +X.
8 m wide bay mates to 4 m or 8 m; same pivot law.
1 m pier; arcade springs from pier sockets.
2 m aisle run parallel to nave; floor and wall share the 2 m offset.
4 m and 2 m floors; flooded vs raised as variants, same pivot.
Ivy/root snap to wall face sockets; tree/reed snap to floor sockets.
Collapsed bay sits on floor sockets, orthogonal to the plan.

uvStrategy.kitPolicy: Trim sheet carries ashlar courses, waterline, and arcade profiles for all modular walls. Unique UVs only for west front, surviving vaulted bay, fallen slabs, and nave tree. Stack modular islands. Do not unique-unwrap every 4 m wall.
uvStrategy.trim: Waterline, course heights, arcade inner profile, pier wrap.
uvStrategy.unique: West front, hero vault, fallen bay, tree.
uvStrategy.texelNote: Lock texel across the stone family so wet/dry and trim/unique match at seams.
uvStrategy.uv2: Only if a Source handoff is named later. Not required for blockout.

flood.notes: Both land on the 0.5 m grid. Waterline trim is continuous through standing and broken walls. Pivots at dry floor grid, not at water surface.
